label: In-process scoreAdvisorPrompt is directly measurable without repo test tooling (Node module.registerHooks maps failing .js specifiers to .ts siblings); on every cross-checkable probe its top-1 equals the daemon's first recommendation (rr-iter3-061 system-spec-kit, rr-iter2-022 memory:save, rr-iter3-168 system-spec-kit); all 217 calls took 2716 ms warm (~12.5 ms/call), discharging iteration 8's daemon-as-proxy caveat for these rows.

The full 217-row engine-level pass (195 labeled + 22 harder) runs in approximately 3.9 s warm total - 2.72 s for 217 in-process scoreAdvisorPrompt calls plus 1.14 s for one ratchet-exact Python subprocess over all 217 prompts - inside the ratchet's own 60 s hook-timeout budget; the pass needs no new harness, only CI wiring.

Engine-level ledger reconciliation: the union yields exactly 73 divergences (68 labeled + 5 harder); the ledger matches on ids, prompt hashes, local tops and counts (0 new drift, 0 resolved, 0 orphans, 0 hash mismatches); exactly one entry fails rule (c): rr-iter3-168, ledgered nativeTop system-deep-loop vs today's system-spec-kit.

rr-iter3-168 is native-engine drift after approval, not a bridge-vs-daemon client split: the live daemon returns system-spec-kit first (0.8251) with system-deep-loop second (0.825) and ambiguous=true, agreeing with the in-process scorer; the entry was approved 2026-09-19 and last edited 2026-09-17, fusion.ts last changed 2026-09-30 (3a4d1a8927), and the fixture's last update (2026-10-10, 479186cfed) does not touch this entry.

At the 0.82 floor a top-1 decision can rest on about 1e-4: on rr-iter3-168 the daemon's top-1 margin is 0.0001 confidence (0.8251 vs 0.825; raw score 0.567677 vs 0.567376) with a third candidate at 0.82 and ambiguous=true - measured evidence that strict top-1 parity is right but needs the floor/ambiguity diagnostic recorded and the ratchet's review semantics for near-floor ledger changes.

Cost/honesty synthesis: the engine-level gate already exists and costs about 3.9 s warm for the full union; today it carries one honest review item (rr-iter3-168); and 43 of 73 divergences (59%) are local abstention (none) vs a native route, so the result should be reported by class rather than as a single agreement rate dominated by the local scorer's abstention behavior.
Node v26 module.registerHooks with a .js-to-.ts fallback plus built-in type stripping makes the TS scorer directly executable in-process; no repo test tooling was needed for the full-union pass.

A divergence ledger is only honest while every dimension it records is re-checked by its gate; a nativeTop recorded once and never re-run decays silently (rr-iter3-168, approved 2026-09-19, stale against both native clients today).
